description:
Telegram bot integration using Bot API over HTTPS:

Polling thread (src/telegram.c):
- telegram_poll_loop(config, message_callback): runs forever in its own thread

- Parses response with cJSON: extract chat_id, text, update_id, from.id
- Filters by allowed_chat_ids if configured
- On new message: invokes callback with (chat_id, user_text, from_id)
- On error: log, backoff (1s, 2s, 4s... up to 30s), retry

Sending replies (called from worker threads):
- telegram_send_message(config, chat_id, text): POST to sendMessage endpoint
- telegram_send_typing(config, chat_id): POST sendChatAction typing indicator
- Handle message length limit (4096 chars) — split into multiple messages if needed
- Markdown parse_mode for code blocks in responses

Data flow:
- Poll thread receives message -> pushes to a thread-safe queue
- Main/dispatcher reads queue -> spawns or wakes worker thread for that chat_id
- Worker thread calls telegram_send_message directly (blocking, fine)

description:

title: Agent loop (state machine with tool execution)
description:
Core agent loop that runs in each worker thread:

State machine (src/agent.c):
- IDLE: waiting for message from dispatcher
- CALLING_LLM: sending messages to LLM, waiting for response
- EXECUTING_TOOLS: processing tool_calls from LLM response
- SENDING_REPLY: sending final text back to Telegram
- ERROR: recoverable error state, log and return to IDLE

Flow per turn:
1. Receive user message -> add to context history
2. Send typing indicator to Telegram
3. Call LLM with full message history + tool definitions
4. If finish_reason == tool_calls:
   a. For each tool_call: look up tool by name, execute, collect result
   b. Append assistant message (with tool_calls) to history
   c. Append tool result messages to history
   d. Increment iteration counter, check max_tool_iterations
   e. Go to step 3
5. If finish_reason == stop:
   a. Append assistant message to history
   b. Send content as Telegram reply
   c. Persist conversation to SQLite
   d. Return to IDLE

Error handling:
- LLM API error: retry once with backoff, then send error message to user
- Tool execution error: return error as tool result (let LLM recover)
- Max iterations exceeded: send partial response + warning to user

Per-conversation state:
- AgentContext struct persists across turns for same chat_id
- Message history trimmed to max_history_messages (keep system + recent)
- Arena reset between turns (transient allocations freed)

title: Thread dispatcher (message queue + worker pool)
description:
Dispatch incoming Telegram messages to per-conversation worker threads:

Message queue (src/dispatch.c):
- Thread-safe queue: mutex + condvar, linked list of pending messages
- dispatch_push(queue, chat_id, text): called by Telegram poll thread
- dispatch_pop(queue): blocks until message available (worker threads call this)

Worker management:
- Worker pool: fixed array of worker slots (e.g., MAX_WORKERS=4 for Pogoplug RAM constraints)
- Each worker owns: AgentContext, CURL handle, arena, assigned chat_id
- Dispatch logic:
  - If chat_id already has an active worker: queue message for that worker
  - If no active worker for chat_id: assign to idle worker (or wait if all busy)
  - If all workers busy and queue full: send 'busy' reply to Telegram

Worker lifecycle:
- Worker thread loops: pop message -> run agent turn -> back to waiting
- Worker can be reassigned to different chat_id when idle (LRU eviction of context)
- On reassignment: persist old context to DB, load new context from DB

Graceful shutdown:
- Main thread sets shutdown flag
- Push sentinel messages to wake all workers
- Join all worker threads
- Flush DB, cleanup curl handles

Memory constraints (Pogoplug has ~128MB RAM):
- MAX_WORKERS=4 (each worker ~2-5MB with history)
- Message queue bounded (drop oldest if overflow, notify user)
- Arena size per worker: 64KB initial, grows as needed
